extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators and compliance personnel for bulk gasoline terminals, bulk gasoline plants, pipeline pumping stations, and environmental compliance consultants/regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and reporting/operational standards under 40 CFR part 63, subpart BBBBBB (gasoline distribution): what facilities must monitor, record, and report, plus applicability, definitions, emission limits, and management practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess emissions report — required events and elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner or operator of an affected source subject to the control requirements shall submit an excess emissions report at the time the semiannual compliance report is submitted. Excess emissions events and the information to include are specified in paragraphs (c)(2)(i) through (v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reporting each instance of: (i) a non-vapor-tight gasoline cargo tank loading where steps to assure it would not be reloaded before vapor-tightness documentation was obtained; (ii) reloading of a non-vapor-tight gasoline cargo tank before vapor tightness documentation obtained per §63.11094(b); (iii) each exceedance or failure to maintain monitored operating parameter value determined under §63.11092(b) (include monitoring data for the days of exceedances and description/timing of repair or maintenance steps); (v) for equipment leaks with no repair within 5 days or not completed within 15 days, report date detected, dates of each repair attempt, reasons for delay, and date of successful repair. (Paragraph (c)(2)(iv) reserved.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual excess emissions report — bulk plants/pumping stations conditional requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator of a bulk gasoline plant or pipeline pumping station shall submit a semiannual excess emissions report including the information specified in (c)(1)(iii) and (c)(2)(v) only for a 6-month period during which an excess emission event has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no excess emission events occurred during the previous 6-month period, no report is required for that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual report — general facility information
rubrics_metrics.description: On or after May 8, 2027, semiannual reports must include general facility information specified in (d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report: (i) Facility name; (ii) Facility physical address (city, county, State); (iii) Latitude/longitude in decimal degrees with at least five decimal places; (iv) Contact person info (name, mailing address, telephone, email); (v) Type of facility (detailed categories e.g., bulk gasoline plant <4,000 gpd, terminal ≥250,000 gpd, pipeline breakout station, pipeline pumping station); (vi) Date of report and beginning/ending dates of reporting period (date of report not required if submitted via CEDRI); (vii) Statement by a responsible official with name, title, and signature certifying truth/accuracy/completeness (CEDRI electronic signature replaces handwritten signature).

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS deviations reporting — temperature CPMS/pressure CPMS/TOC CEMS
rubrics_metrics.description: For each thermal oxidation system monitored by temperature CPMS, each pressure CPMS under §60.502a(h), and each vapor recovery system subject to table 3, report CMS-related deviations as specified in (d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 3-hour rolling averages are below operating limit or pressure/TOC exceed limits: report date & start time of deviation; duration in hours; each 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature, average pressure, or 3-hour rolling average TOC concentration (indicate whether methane excluded for TOC); a unique identifier for the CMS; make, model, and date of last calibration check; cause of deviation and corrective action taken. For outages or CPMS/CEMS not operating/out of control when liquid product loaded: report date & start time; duration in hours; unique identifier; make/model/date of last calibration; cause and corrective action. For TOC CEMS outages using the limited alternative (§60.504a(e)), include indication of limited alternative use and either a statement of no deviations while using the limited alternative or counts of specific deviation types during limited alternative use: number of adsorption cycles exceeding quantity limits; number of desorption cycles with vacuum pressure below average; number of desorption cycles with purge gas below average; number of desorption cycles with vacuum/purge cycle duration less than average (enter 0 if none).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting for thermal oxidation systems and flares — operating parameter/visible emission deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report for each thermal oxidation system complying via §63.11092(e)(2)(ii) and each flare used per table 3: specified instances and detailed info in (d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report date, start and end times for: (A) each 15-minute block with at least 1 minute when gasoline vapors routed to flare and no pilot flame present; (B) each 2-hour period with visible emissions exceeding total of 5 minutes (report minutes observed or best-estimate cumulative minutes); (C) each 15-minute period when operating limits in §63.670(d)-(f) not met (identify specific limit not met). For (C) additional reporting depends on monitoring approach: (1) if using loading rate limits (per §60.502a(c)(3)(vii)), report required min ratio and actual ratio of gasoline loaded to total product for the rolling 15-minute period, and required min quantity and actual gallons if applicable; (2) if using supplemental gas flow rate monitoring (§60.502a(c)(3)(viii)), report required min supplemental gas flow rate and actual supplemental gas flow rate including units for the 15-minute block; (3) if using other parameter monitoring systems, report net heating value operating parameter(s) during deviation determined per §63.670(k)-(n). Also report start date/time/duration in minutes for each period when vapors were routed to flare/TO and applicable monitoring was not performed. For CMS-involved instances report unique identifier, make/model/date of last calibration, cause of deviation/downtime and corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report loading without vapor tightness documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report any instance where liquid product was loaded into a gasoline cargo tank for which vapor tightness documentation required under §63.11094(b) was not provided or available in the terminal's records (d)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cargo tank owner and address; cargo tank identification number; date and time of loading without proper documentation; date proper documentation received or statement that proper documentation was never received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report loading into tanks not using submerged filling or not properly connected
rubrics_metrics.description: For each instance when liquid product was loaded into gasoline cargo tanks not using submerged filling, not equipped with compatible vapor collection/balancing equipment, or not properly connected to the terminal's vapor collection/plant balancing system, report the items in (d)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report date/time of the loading; the type of deviation (e.g., not submerged filling, incompatible equipment, not properly connected); cargo tank identification number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report improper vapor balancing between cargo tanks and storage tanks
rubrics_metrics.description: For each instance when gasoline was loaded between gasoline cargo tanks and storage tanks and the plant's vapor balancing system was not properly connected, report the items in (d)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report date/time of loading that was not properly connected; cargo tank and storage tank identification numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak inspection and leak reporting details
rubrics_metrics.description: Report information for each leak inspection and each leak identified under §63.11089(c) and §60.503a(a)(2) as specified in (d)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For leaks detected during required leak inspections: report date of inspection; leak determination method (OGI or Method 21); total number and type of equipment with leaks detected; total number/type repaired within 15 calendar days; total number/type with no repair attempt within 5 calendar days; total number/type placed on delay of repair per §60.502a(j)(8). For leaks identified by audio/visual/olfactory methods during normal duties: report total number/type identified, number/type repaired within 15 days, number/type with no repair attempt within 5 days, number/type placed on delay of repair. Also report total number of leaks on the delay-of-repair list at start and end of reporting period. For each leak on the delay-of-repair list at any time during the period report unique equipment ID, type of equipment, leak determination method (OGI, Method 21, or audio/visual/olfactory), reasons repair not feasible within 15 days, and if applicable date repair was completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gasoline storage tank reporting and LEL monitoring deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: For gasoline storage tanks subject to item 2 of table 1, report the information specified in (d)(8) depending on compliance option and any deviations in LEL monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If complying with options 2(a), 2(b), or 2(d) in table 1, report information specified in §60.115b(a)/(b) or deviations per §60.115b(c) as applicable, or if complying with option 2(e) report per §63.1066(b). If complying with options 2(c) or 2(e), for each deviation in LEL monitoring report: date and start/end times of LEL monitoring and tank being monitored; description of monitoring event (e.g., concurrent with visual inspection, occurred on a different date, re-monitoring due to high winds, re-monitoring after repair attempt); wind speed in mph at top of tank on monitoring date; highest 5-minute rolling average reading during event; whether floating roof was repaired/replaced/taken out of service. If repaired/replaced, also report info for each re-monitoring conducted to confirm the repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deviations statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If there were no deviations from emission limitations, operating parameters, or work practice standards during the reporting period, provide a statement to that effect (d)(9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there were no periods during which a continuous monitoring system (including a CEMS or CPMS) was inoperable or out-of-control, provide a statement that no such CMS inoperability/out-of-control periods occurred during the reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual report submission method and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission requirements for semiannual reports are specified in (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each owner/operator must submit semiannual compliance reports with information in paragraph (c) or (d) to the Administrator per §63.13. Beginning May 8, 2027, or once the report template for this subpart has been available on the CEDRI website for one year (whichever later), all subsequent semiannual compliance reports must be submitted using the appropriate electronic report template on CEDRI and following §63.9(k). Any mailed medium must be sent to the attention of the Gasoline Distribution Sector Lead. The date templates become available will be listed on CEDRI. Unless Administrator or delegated authority approves a different schedule, reports must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart regardless of submission method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which General Provisions apply (Table 4 mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 4 to this subpart lists which parts of the General Provisions (40 CFR part 63) apply to this subpart, with brief descriptions and yes/no applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 4 lists many General Provisions (e.g., §63.1 Applicability — Yes; §63.6(e)(1)(i) General duty to minimize emissions — No, see §63.11085; §63.6(f)(2) Methods for determining compliance — Yes; §63.7 QA/Test Plan — Yes; §63.8 monitoring requirements and performance specifications — Yes; etc.). Use Table 4 to determine which general provisions and procedures (notifications, testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, reporting) apply to compliance under subpart BBBBBB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-delegable authority — electronic reporting alternative approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities that cannot be delegated to State, local, or Tribal agencies include those specified in §63.11099(c)(1) through (5), including approval of an alternative to any electronic reporting to EPA required by this subpart (c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of alternatives to EPA-required electronic reporting must be made by the Administrator and cannot be delegated to State/local/Tribal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Bulk gasoline terminal (pre- and post-May 8, 2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bulk gasoline terminal means: (1) prior to May 8, 2027, any gasoline storage and distribution facility that receives gasoline by pipeline, ship or barge, or cargo tank and has a gasoline throughput of 20,000 gallons per day or greater; (2) on or after May 8, 2027, any gasoline facility which receives gasoline by pipeline, ship, barge, or cargo tank and subsequently loads all or a portion of the gasoline into gasoline cargo tanks for transport ... and has a gasoline throughput of 20,000 gallons per day (75,700 liters per day) or greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gasoline throughput is the maximum calculated design throughput as may be limited by enforceable conditions and discoverable by the Administrator and any other person. Post-May 8, 2027 definition emphasizes loading into cargo tanks for transport and provides the liter equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Flare
rubrics_metrics.description: Flare means a thermal combustion device using an open or shrouded flame (without full enclosure) such that the pollutants are not emitted through a conveyance suitable to conduct a performance test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes flares from thermal oxidation systems (which are enclosed and have conveyances suitable for performance tests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Gasoline (Reid vapor pressure threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline means any petroleum distillate or petroleum distillate/alcohol blend having a Reid vapor pressure of 4.0 pounds per square inch (27.6 kilopascals) or greater, which is used as a fuel for internal combustion engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines which products are subject to the subpart's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Operating parameter value
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating parameter value means a value for an operating or emission parameter of the vapor processing system (e.g., temperature) which, if maintained continuously by itself or in combination with one or more other operating parameter values, determines that an owner or operator has complied with the applicable emission standard. The value is determined using procedures in §63.11092(b) and (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to establish monitored parameter limits for compliance demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Pipeline breakout station
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline breakout station means: (1) prior to May 8, 2027, a facility along a pipeline containing storage vessels used to relieve surges or receive and store gasoline from the pipeline for reinjection and continued transportation by pipeline or to other facilities; (2) on or after May 8, 2027, a facility along a pipeline containing storage vessels used to relieve surges or receive and store gasoline from the pipeline for reinjection and continued transportation by pipeline to other facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pipeline breakout stations do not have loading racks where gasoline is loaded into cargo tanks; if any gasoline is loaded into cargo tanks and facility throughput exceeds the terminal limits, the facility is treated as a bulk gasoline terminal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Pipeline pumping station
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline pumping station means a facility along a pipeline containing pumps to maintain desired pressure and flow of product through the pipeline, and not containing gasoline loading racks or gasoline storage tanks other than surge control tanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates pumping stations from terminals and breakout stations for applicability purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Thermal oxidation system
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermal oxidation system means an enclosed combustion device used to mix and ignite fuel, air pollutants, and air to provide a flame to heat and oxidize hazardous air pollutants. Auxiliary fuel may be used. Thermal oxidation systems emit pollutants through a conveyance suitable to conduct a performance test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify control technology (table 3) and associated reporting/monitoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage tanks — small tank requirements (Table 1, item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you own/operate a gasoline storage tank with (i) capacity <75 m3; or (ii) capacity <151 m3 and throughput ≤480 gpd, then you must: equip each tank with a fixed roof mounted stationary and maintain all openings closed when not in use; and no later than dates in §63.11083, set pressure relief devices on each tank to no less than 18 inches of water to minimize breathing losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gallons per day calculated by summing current day's throughput plus previous 364 days, divided by 365. Compliance dates in §63.11083 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage tanks — larger tanks requirements (Table 1, item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For gasoline storage tanks with capacity ≥75 m3 and not meeting item 1 criteria, owners/operators must comply with one of multiple options and management practices in item 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: (a) reduce TOC by 95 weight-percent with closed vent and control device per §60.112b(a)(3); or (b) equip internal floating roof per §60.112b(a)(1) (with some exceptions); (c) operate internal floating roof control system to maintain vapor concentration above the roof at or below 25% LEL on a 5-minute rolling average without purge gas; (d) equip external floating roof per §60.112b(a)(2) (with phased requirements); (e) equip/operate internal & external floating roofs per §63.1063(a)(1)/(b) (with some secondary seal exceptions) and meet schedule in §63.11083; and (f) maintain vapor concentration ≤25% LEL as in (c). Some options may require additional controls beyond cited sections to meet the 25% LEL requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surge control tanks — requirements (Table 1, item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a surge control tank, equip each tank with a fixed roof mounted in a stationary manner and with a pressure/vacuum vent with positive cracking pressure ≥0.50 inches of water, and maintain all openings closed when not in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple mechanical requirements intended to minimize breathing losses and emissions from surge control tanks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large bulk gasoline terminal loading rack requirements (Table 2, item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you own/operate a bulk gasoline terminal loading rack(s) with total throughput ≥250,000 gpd (large bulk gasoline terminal), then you must implement several vapor control and operational requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (a) equip loading racks with a vapor collection system designed and operated to collect TOC vapors displaced during loading; (b) reduce TOC emissions to ≤80 mg/l of gasoline loaded into cargo tanks at the loading rack; (c) by dates in §63.11083 reduce TOC to limits in table 3 (1(b) does not apply when demonstrating compliance with item 1(c)); (d) design/operate vapor collection to prevent TOC vapors collected at one rack/lane from passing through another rack/lane to atmosphere; (e) limit loading into vapor-tight gasoline cargo tanks using procedures in §60.502(e)-(j) (term 'tank truck' means 'gasoline cargo tank'); (f) by dates in §63.11083 limit loading of liquid product into gasoline cargo tanks using procedures in §60.502a(e)-(i) and §63.11092(g),(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller bulk gasoline terminal loading rack requirements (Table 2, item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If loading rack throughput (total of all racks) is less than 250,000 gpd, owners/operators must use submerged filling and make throughput records available on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (a) use submerged filling with submerged fill pipe no more than 6 inches from bottom of cargo tank; (b) make records available within 24 hours of Administrator request to document throughput; (c) by dates in §63.11083, limit loading of gasoline into vapor-tight cargo tanks using procedures in §60.502a(e) and §63.11092(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limitations and control-specific requirements for large terminals (Table 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 3 sets emission limits and operational requirements for large bulk gasoline terminals based on the control system used (thermal oxidation, flare, carbon adsorption/refrigerated condenser/other vapor recovery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1. Thermal oxidation system: (a) reduce TOC to ≤35 mg/l of liquid product loaded into cargo tanks at the rack; (b) continuously meet applicable operating limit in §63.11092(e)(2). 2. Flare: operate the flare following applicable requirements in §60.502a(c)(3). 3. Carbon adsorption/refrigerated condenser/other vapor recovery: (a) reduce TOC to ≤19,200 ppmv as propane determined on a 3-hour rolling average considering all periods when system capable of processing vapors (including during loading and carbon bed regeneration); (b) operate system to minimize air or nitrogen intrusion except as needed for design/operation (use of diluents to meet standards is prohibited under §63.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring system applicability and operation (reference to §63.8 and §63.8(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring requirements and performance specifications in §63.8 apply to the subpart as indicated in Table 4; monitoring systems must be operated and maintained consistent with good air pollution control practices as per §63.8(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where monitoring is required, owners/operators must follow performance specifications in appendix B to part 60, install monitoring on each affected source unless combined monitoring is sufficient, and maintain QA/QC, operation, and maintenance per §63.8 subsections. Multiple monitoring systems on an emission point must report all results unless a system is a backup.
